items.stem: Why is it misleading to treat the whole of East Asia as culturally identical to China?

options.text: Korea, Japan and others adapted shared influences into distinct institutions and identities
options.rationale: Correct: borrowing was selective and reworked, producing real divergence.

options.text: Because China had no influence on the region
options.rationale: Its influence was large; the error is erasing local difference.
They interacted extensively; the point is they still differed.

options.text: Because they shared no writing or ideas
options.rationale: They shared much, yet developed distinctly.

items.stem: A student explains rapid post-1945 East Asian growth 'purely because of culture'. What is the weakness?

options.text: It ignores specific policies, institutions, global conditions and historical contingency that shaped growth
options.rationale: Correct: culture-only explanations overlook state policy, timing and external factors.
Culture may matter, but it cannot be the sole explanation.
Substantial growth occurred; the issue is explaining it.
